# Migrate the ECS backend from DefaultEcs to Arch, behind a MonoDreams-owned facade

**Origem:** https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/issues/119 (the issue is the complete brief; this plan is the issue **plus the live-codebase verification deltas** below — where they disagree, this plan wins because it was measured)
**Branch sugerida:** `issue-119-wave0` → `issue-119-wave1` → `issue-119-wave2` → `issue-119-wave3` → `issue-119-wave4` — **five stacked branches, one PR per wave** (issue §10: "Each wave is its own PR. Do not squash waves together."). Each branch is created from the previous wave's branch; PRs are opened sequentially with the previous wave's branch as base, retargeted to `main` as predecessors merge.
**Domínios:** foundation (**sensitive**), rendering, rendering-text, camera, physics, collision, level-loading, level-ldtk, ui, cursor, dialogue, debug, level-editor, audio, examples, cli, platform, tests
**Tier de risco:** deep-plan — engine-wide flow replacement crossing all 14 modules, rooted in the sensitive `foundation` domain; the PR-create gate (`.claude/hooks/deep-plan-pr-gate.sh`) will trip on every wave.
**Status:** DRAFT

---

## 1. Context

DefaultEcs (pinned `0.18.0-beta01`) is unmaintained and carries a live correctness bug (#117:
`EntityQueryFilterFactory` cache-key collision; #118 landed a workaround, not a cure). The issue
decides: ship **(1)** `MonoDreams.Ecs`, an engine-owned facade in the `foundation` module that
becomes the ONLY ECS surface for every other module, Examples, Demos, CLI-scaffolded games and
tests; then **(2)** swap the facade's backend from DefaultEcs to
[Arch](https://github.com/genaray/Arch). Behaviour is preserved; only ECS plumbing moves.
Non-goals: gameplay/module logic rewrites, component-shape changes, Arch.Relationships /
Arch.Persistence, renderer changes.

Read issue #119 §1–§5 for the full rationale, the measured API-usage table, and hazards H1–H10.
This plan does not restate them; it corrects and extends them.

## 2. Verification deltas (measured on `main` @ `7b2cbe2a`, 2026-08-18)

Three Explore agents + direct `rg` verified every load-bearing claim. The issue's coverage table
is **incomplete**; the following must be treated as part of the brief.

### 2a. Surfaces the issue's table MISSES (each needs a facade shape)

| # | Missing surface | Measured | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **Value-predicate queries** `.With((in T c) => …)` | 2 sites: `MonoDreams/physics/System/GravitySystem.cs:10`, `MonoDreams/rendering/System/Draw/MasterRenderSystem.cs:90` (`BuildDrawSet`) | Arch has NO value-predicate filter. Documented engine premise (foundation — "A value-predicate `EntitySet` re-evaluates only when the component is published"): predicate runs **only on publication** (`Set`/`NotifyChanged`), cached as membership. The facade must own publication-driven predicate membership — the single highest-risk item of the migration. |
| M2 | **`entity.NotifyChanged<T>()`** | ~40 sites across cursor, ui, debug, level-editor, tests | The engine's publication verb: re-runs predicate sets AND fires Changed subscriptions with `old == new` (AudioSystem relies on `ReferenceEquals(old,new)` to detect notify-style publications — `AudioSystem.cs:141`). Facade must own it. |
| M3 | **`[Subscribe]` attribute + `world.Subscribe(this)`** | 17 `[Subscribe]` handlers across 14 files; 9 `Subscribe(this)` registration sites (plus 19 typed `Subscribe<T>` sites) | The facade message bus must support BOTH registration forms: typed `Subscribe<T>(handler)` → `IDisposable`, and attribute-scanned `Subscribe(object)` (reflection over `[Subscribe]` methods, AOT-safe — no IL emit). |
| M4 | **`ParallelSystem<T>`** | 5 uses, all in `MonoDreams/level-editor/Composition/EditorPipelineRegistrar.cs` (:376–379 etc.) | Facade must own it (like `SequentialSystem`). Note all hosts create `DefaultParallelRunner(1)` — degree 1 — so a correct sequential implementation behind the same name is behaviour-preserving. |
| M5 | **World components: 4 types, not 2, and world-level `Remove<T>()`** | `LDtkLevelDataComponent`, `EntityHierarchy`, **`CurrentLevelComponent`**, **`CurrentBackgroundColorComponent`**; 6 world-`Remove` sites (`LDtkLevelLoadSystem.cs:71,80,81`, `EditorTransport.cs:399,400,411,412`) | The facade singleton store needs `Set/Get/Has/Remove` + Added/Removed/Changed notifications. The Restart transport semantics (`Set` over present component fires *Changed* not *Added* — CORE_TENETS §9) must be preserved exactly. |
| M6 | **`SubscribeEntityComponentChanged` handler carries `(in Entity, in T old, in T new)`** | `BoundaryBakeSystem.cs:97`, `AudioSystem.cs:42`, `TileGridBakeSystem.cs:159` | Arch's Set events (even when compiled in) do NOT deliver the old value. Facade-fired events are the only design that can honour this signature → hardens the H7 decision (D1 below). |
| M7 | **`IGameScreen` exposes `ISystem<GameState>`** (`MonoDreams/foundation/Screen/GameScreen.cs:11-13`) | every screen implements it; 71 engine files reference `ISystem<GameState>` | The public screen contract itself must move to the facade's `ISystem<T>`. |
| M8 | **`ReadAllComponents`: 3 sites, not 2** | + `MonoDreams.Examples.Core/Inspector/ComponentIntrospector.cs:9,39` | All three go through the facade's `IComponentReader` port. |
| M9 | **Packaging: 4 csproj + lockfile + schema doc** | `MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj:143`, `MonoDreams.Examples.Core:38`, `MonoDreams.Demos:25`, **`scratchpad/blazor-spike/MonoDreams.Spike:58`** (git-tracked, out of sln); `MonoDreams/packages.lock.json:11`; `MonoDreams/module.schema.json:55` (doc example); `MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj:31-33` (comment) | Wave 4's "zero DefaultEcs" sweep covers all of these. The obsolete blazor spike is **deleted** in wave 4 (decision D7). |
| M10 | **Reactive callback doing structural mutation inside the publish path** | `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.cs:89,94` — `entity.Set<ColliderTagComponent>()` from inside a `ComponentAdded` handler; its subscription `IDisposable`s are discarded (:74-75) | Hardest single case under an archetype backend: a structural move triggered *during* a component add. The facade's event dispatch must make this safe (deferral or dispatch-after-move), and must define whether discarding the subscription handle is legal. |
| M11 | **`MonoDreams.Cli` module registry + scaffolded games** | CLI not in sln; `monodreams init` scaffolds heads that `new World(...)` | Scaffolder templates and the registry must emit facade usings/packages; manifest-honesty CI proves it per module. |

### 2b. Corrections DOWNWARD (less work than the issue claims)

- **`SystemProfiler` needs zero migration** — it is a static class feeding `GatedSystem.TimingSink`; no DefaultEcs reference at all.
- **`ISuspendableSystem` has no DefaultEcs coupling** (interface is pure; one cast site in `GatedSystem.cs:130`).
- **`EntityQuery.Count` is NOT a required capability** — the one apparent `.Count` hit is a `HashSet<Entity>`, not an `EntitySet`. Required surface: construct-once, `With<T>`/`Without<T>`/value-predicate, `GetEntities()` snapshot enumeration valid within the frame, first-match-and-break, transient `using`-disposable queries, `Dispose()`.
- **`DrawPrepSystemBase` is dead code** — zero subclasses, and its `useParallel` param actually maps to DefaultEcs `useBuffer`. Delete in wave 1 instead of porting.
- **Structural-mutation surface differs in shape from H2's "at least 10 subclasses"**: 3 unsafe engine `AEntitySetSystem` sites (`CullingSystem.cs:100,107`, `ButtonMeshPrepSystem.cs:83`, `TextPrepSystem.cs:75`) + `GameOverSystem` (Examples; creates AND disposes mid-iteration) + ~6 unsafe manual-iteration sites (`SelectionSystem.cs:404-415` +4 more, `TabSystem.cs:71-77`, `DialogSystem.cs:38-51`, `TileGridPaintSystem.cs:162`, `HudPreviewSystem.cs:74`) + the M10 callback. ~7 editor systems already buffer-then-mutate (the pattern to generalize). A facade-level snapshot-iteration guarantee covers all of them.
- **`ScreenController` RECEIVES an `IParallelRunner`** (ctor param, re-exposed as `Runner`); hosts create `DefaultParallelRunner(1)`. Only 9 system types across 5 files consume a runner.
- **Demos has 6 screens** (`camera`, `physics`, `dialogue`, `ui`, `audio`, `launcher`), not 4; `--exit` is a no-op (exit is driven by `--frames`). Acceptance criteria updated accordingly.
- **The solution file is lowercase `monodreams.sln`**; verification commands must use it.
- **No benchmark project exists** — wave 0 builds it from scratch; no BenchmarkDotNet reference anywhere today.

### 2c. Repo facts the waves must honour

- **Conventions:** commits/PRs in **English**, Conventional Commits `type(scope): description`; branch naming `issue-<N>` per history. No enforced formatter. Core builds before heads (MGCB absolute-path rule).
- **Guard-test model:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/EditorThemeLintTests.cs` (git-tracked source scan, comment-stripping, allowlist) + the `ManifestHonestyTests` KnownGaps ratchet (fails in three directions: fixed→delete, shrunk→narrow, new-behind-known→fail).
- **Process-wide state:** `MonoDreams.Tests/ProcessWideState.cs` + `ProcessWideStateGuardAttribute` (assembly scope) + `DeterministicCollectionOrderer`. **No DefaultEcs statics are tracked today.** Any facade/Arch static (component-type registry, `World.Worlds`, query caches) must be registered in `ProcessWideState` in the PR that introduces it (H9).
- **CI:** `ci.yml` = `xvfb-run dotnet test --configuration Release -m:1 -p:RestoreDisableParallel=true`; `manifest-honesty.yml` = per-module scaffold+add+build matrix derived from `ls MonoDreams/*/module.json`.
- **CHANGELOG format:** `## Unreleased` → `### Breaking — <lowercase summary> ([#119](…))` + prose + bullets with inline `*Migration:*` clauses.
- **Premises naming DefaultEcs to rewrite** (wave 2/4): foundation (file preamble :7; ISuspendable :393; process-wide :505; **value-predicate premise :692 — rewrite entirely against the facade contract**), collision (:223 `[Subscribe]` semantics), audio (:14, :207 version-pinned pub/sub claim; overview :42), rendering (:772 `AsSet()` lifecycle), level-editor (:1260 composites; :1509 `ReadAllComponents`; overview :29,:66), ui (:988,:993), dialogue (:222), camera (:235 + overview :30 + `docs/flows/camera.md:83` — iteration-order claims are DefaultEcs-specific).
- **Env:** .NET SDK 8.0.416 with `wasm-tools` installed — the wave-0 web leg is runnable on this machine.

## 3. Recorded design decisions (autonomous, per issue defaults + verification)

- **D1 (H7): facade-fired reactive notifications — option (a).** The facade owns `Set/Add/Remove/Destroy/SetSingleton/NotifyChanged`, so it raises the engine's events itself; Arch's `EVENTS`-flag events stay off. Mandatory, not just preferred: Changed carries `(old, new)` (M6), `NotifyChanged` must fire Changed with `old==new` (M2), and predicate membership (M1) needs a publication hook anyway. Vendoring Arch with `EVENTS` (option b) stays the documented fallback.
- **D2 (H2): `EntitySystem<T>` iterates a materialized snapshot buffer** — structural changes (Set-new/Remove/Dispose/Create) during `Update` stay safe, matching today's tolerated behaviour. Documented as a facade premise. The ~7 already-buffered editor systems keep their local buffers (no churn).
- **D3 (H3): `EntityQuery` maintains publication-driven materialized membership** (updated by the facade's own add/remove/publish events), enumeration hands out a frame-stable snapshot; transient `using` queries supported. `Count` deliberately unimplemented until a consumer exists.
- **D4: the facade keeps DefaultEcs-shaped names** — `entity.Set` (add-or-update, H1), `entity.Get<T>()` → `ref T`, `entity.Has/Remove`, `entity.Dispose()`, `entity.IsAlive` (property), `world.CreateEntity()`, `world.Subscribe/Publish`, `Subscribe(Entity|World)Component*`, `NotifyChanged` — so wave 1 is dominated by `using` swaps, and the 1826 `Set` call sites never see Arch's update-only `Set` (guard-enforced).
- **D5: five stacked PRs** opened sequentially without waiting for merges; user merges in order. Wave N+1's PR base = wave N's branch. *(Confirm at approval.)*
- **D6: Arch.Extended adoption:** `Arch.AOT.SourceGenerator` yes (console/iOS AOT); `Arch.System.SourceGenerator` optional and only in wave 3 if benchmarks justify; `Arch.EventBus`/`Persistence`/`Relationships`/`LowLevel` no.
- **D7: `scratchpad/blazor-spike/` is deleted in wave 4** — it was the KNI/Blazor investigation that has since landed as `MonoDreams.Examples.Web`; keeping it would either violate the zero-DefaultEcs acceptance criterion or force pointless migration of a spike. *(Confirm at approval.)*
- **D8: upstream note** — after wave 4 merges, comment on Doraku/DefaultEcs#197 and close #117 with the outcome. Outward-facing; *(confirm at approval)*.

## 4. Waves

### Wave 0 — spike & baseline (branch `issue-119-wave0`, PR base `main`)

No engine code changes. Deliverables:
1. **`MonoDreams.Benchmarks`** (BenchmarkDotNet, net8.0, added to `monodreams.sln`): entity creation, structural churn (add/remove component), iteration over 10k/100k/1M entities; a struct-component case and a managed-`DrawComponent`-shaped case; **DefaultEcs vs Arch side by side** (both packages referenced here only). Baseline numbers recorded in `MonoDreams.Benchmarks/RESULTS.md` and the PR body.
2. **Target proofs** for Arch: a spike console sample builds+runs desktop; a KNI/BlazorGL web build of a Blazor head referencing Arch compiles (`-p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web` analog); an AOT publish (`PublishAot=true`) smoke test with `Arch.AOT.SourceGenerator`.
3. **H7 proof:** a runnable sample demonstrating facade-fired Added/Changed(old,new)/Removed + world-singleton notifications + predicate-set membership over Arch, exercising the M10 shape (structural mutation from inside a handler).
4. Findings written to the PR; **if the spike invalidates part of this plan, the plan is amended before wave 1** (explicitly allowed to say so).

Acceptance: full gate green (`dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj && dotnet test --configuration Release`); benchmark project runs; findings + numbers in PR body.

### Wave 1 — facade with DefaultEcs backend (branch `issue-119-wave1`)

1. `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/` implements `MonoDreams.Ecs` covering issue §4 **plus M1–M8**, delegating to DefaultEcs: `World`/`Entity` (aliased), `EcsWorld.Create()` factory (H10), `EntityQuery` (+ value predicates), `EntitySystem<T>` (reads `[With]`/`[Without]` attributes), `SequentialSystem`/`ParallelSystem`/`ActionSystem`/`AComponentSystem`, `ISystem<T>`, `IParallelRunner` + a default runner, message bus (typed + `[Subscribe]` forms), world singletons (4 types incl. `Remove`), reactive subscriptions (all 5 verbs, exact handler signatures), `NotifyChanged`, `ReadAllComponents(IComponentReader)`.
2. All ~321 files (engine 176, tests 100, Examples.Core 34, Demos 7, heads 4) migrate to `MonoDreams.Ecs`. Delete `DrawPrepSystemBase` (dead). `IGameScreen` moves to facade types (M7).
3. **Guard test `MonoDreams.Tests/Architecture/EcsBoundaryLintTests.cs`** (modeled on `EditorThemeLintTests` + KnownGaps ratchet): no git-tracked `.cs` outside `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/` (and outside `scratchpad/`, until D7 deletes it) may reference `DefaultEcs` (nor, from wave 2, `Arch.`); ratchet empty at wave close.
4. New facade premises land in `MonoDreams/foundation/docs/premises.md` (Set add-or-update; snapshot iteration; query lifetime; publication contract now owned by the facade; iteration order unspecified unless sorted).
5. **Zero behaviour change**: full-solution Release gate green ×5 consecutive runs; `MONODREAMS_TEST_SEED=8` green; headless Demos screenshots **byte-identical** to a `main` baseline captured the same way, all 6 screens.

### Wave 2 — swap the backend to Arch (branch `issue-119-wave2`)

1. Only `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/` + dependency edits (`MonoDreams.csproj`, `packages.lock.json`, `foundation/module.json` gains Arch alongside DefaultEcs-removal deferred to wave 4 if a transition period helps — default: swap here, single source of truth). Work H1–H10 **plus M1/M2/M3/M5/M6/M10** site by site; every facade static registered in `ProcessWideState`; `ProcessWideStateHygieneTests` extended over Arch statics (H9); tests that leak `new World()` get `using`/dispose.
2. **All 11 reactive sites verified working by a test each** (issue §9), including the M10 mutation-inside-handler shape and the Restart transport Changed-not-Added semantics (M5).
3. Guard test extended: no raw `Arch.` reference outside `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/`.
4. Acceptance: full gate ×5 + seeded run green; all 6 demo screens headless non-blank + flat heap; Examples desktop boots `Level_0` and `Blender_Level`; editor `.mdscene` save/load round-trip green; web head builds (`-p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web`); pointer-replay PNG diff vs `main` baseline — **every pixel difference explained one by one in the PR (ordering vs regression), never re-baselined blindly** (H4).

### Wave 3 — hot paths (branch `issue-119-wave3`)

1. Convert hot systems to chunk/`ref` queries: `CullingSystem`, `SpritePrepSystem`, `TextPrepSystem`, `MeshPrepSystem`, `YSortSystem`, `MasterRenderSystem` feed, `GravitySystem`, `VelocitySystem`, collision detection (`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.BuildEntries`). Opt-in chunked override on `EntitySystem<T>`; `Arch.System.SourceGenerator` only if measurably better.
2. Acceptance: wave-0 benchmarks re-run — improve or hold vs the wave-2 numbers, reported in the PR; full gate + demos green as in wave 2.

### Wave 4 — cleanup & docs (branch `issue-119-wave4`)

1. Remove DefaultEcs from every csproj/lockfile/`module.json`; update `module.schema.json`'s doc example; delete `scratchpad/blazor-spike/` (D7); regenerate locks.
2. `monodreams init` + `monodreams add <every module>` scaffolds and compiles — manifest-honesty green all legs (`MONODREAMS_MANIFEST_HONESTY=1`); update `KnownGaps` only if a gap genuinely changed.
3. Retire #118's DefaultEcs-specific defensive resets where Arch makes them moot; **keep** the seeded ordering harness and the hygiene guard.
4. Docs sweep (issue §8 + §2c premise list): CORE_TENETS (ECS backend is an implementation detail behind `MonoDreams.Ecs`), foundation overview facade tour, all premises naming DefaultEcs, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/agents/skills-config.md` stack line, `README.md` (+ credits keep the Doraku thank-you, reworded historically), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/web-targeting.md:189`, `docs/index.md`, `docs/flows/camera.md:83`; new `docs/ecs-migration.md` (for module vendorers); `CHANGELOG.md` Breaking entry with `*Migration:*` lines per break.
5. Close #117 with the outcome; note on Doraku/DefaultEcs#197 (D8, user-approved).

## 5. Contract

Atomic, verifiable commitments. "Gate" = `dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj && dotnet test --configuration Release` on `monodreams.sln` (core-first rule). Each item names its protecting test or the artifact that proves it.

**Wave 0**
- C1. `MonoDreams.Benchmarks` exists, in `monodreams.sln`, runs `dotnet run -c Release --project MonoDreams.Benchmarks -- --filter '*'` producing creation/churn/iteration numbers for DefaultEcs AND Arch at 10k/100k/1M, struct + managed cases. Proof: `MonoDreams.Benchmarks/RESULTS.md` committed.
- C2. Arch compiles into a KNI/BlazorGL WASM build and an AOT (`PublishAot=true`) publish on this machine. Proof: spike projects + PR-body command transcript.
- C3. The facade-fired event design (D1) is proven end to end over Arch, including structural mutation from inside an Added handler (M10 shape) and Changed(old,new). Proof: runnable spike + PR write-up.

**Wave 1**
- C4. `MonoDreams.Ecs` exposes the complete surface of issue §4 + M1–M8; every public member XML-documented with its semantic guarantee (add-or-update, snapshot iteration, publication). Test: compile of all consumers + `EcsFacadeContractTests` (new; per-guarantee unit tests: Set add-or-update, NotifyChanged fires Changed old==new, predicate membership updates on publish only, snapshot iteration tolerates Set/Remove/Dispose mid-loop, singleton Set-when-present fires Changed not Added, world Remove fires Removed).
- C5. Zero files outside `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/` reference `DefaultEcs` (scratchpad excluded until deleted). Test: `EcsBoundaryLintTests` (ratchet empty).
- C6. `DrawPrepSystemBase` deleted; no `useParallel/useBuffer` mislabel survives. Test: compile + lint absence.
- C7. Wave-1 behaviour identity: gate green ×5; `MONODREAMS_TEST_SEED=8` green; 6/6 headless demo screens byte-identical PNGs vs the `main` baseline. Proof: PR body with hashes.
- C8. New/updated foundation premises for the facade (Set semantics, iteration snapshot, query lifetime, publication contract, unspecified order), each with `Tests:` naming C4's tests — no new premise ships `Tests: none yet`.

**Wave 2**
- C9. Only `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/` + dependency manifests change (diff-scoped; reviewer-checkable). Proof: PR file list.
- C10. The 11 reactive subscription sites each have a named passing test exercising the real system through the facade (list in issue §3): `LDtkTileParserSystem` ×2, `LDtkEntityParserSystem`, `AudioSystem` ×2, `BoundaryBakeSystem` ×2, `TileGridBakeSystem` ×2, `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` ×2 (incl. tag-Set-inside-Added). Tests: existing suites extended + new `ReactiveSubscriptionSiteTests` where uncovered.
- C11. Value-predicate sets behave per the foundation premise under Arch: in-place mutation without publish does NOT move membership; `Set`/`NotifyChanged` does. Tests: `EcsFacadeContractTests` + `GravitySystem`/`MasterRenderSystem` behaviour tests.
- C12. Every Arch/facade process-wide static is registered in `ProcessWideState`; hygiene tests extended; world-leaking tests fixed with disposal. Test: `ProcessWideStateHygieneTests` (extended).
- C13. `entity.IsAlive`, default/`Entity.Null` handles, and recycled-id behaviour are covered by facade tests (H6). Test: `EcsFacadeContractTests`.
- C14. Guard forbids raw `Arch.` outside the facade. Test: `EcsBoundaryLintTests` (extended).
- C15. Gate ×5 + seeded green; 6/6 demos non-blank + `AssertHeapFlat`; `Blender_Level` + `Level_0` boot; `.mdscene` round-trip; web head builds; pointer-replay diff explained per-pixel-difference in the PR. Proof: PR body.
- C16. Benchmarks re-run: wave-2 Arch numbers vs wave-0 DefaultEcs baseline in the PR body (H8: managed-component cases measured and noted, NOT converted).

**Wave 3**
- C17. Each listed hot system converted to chunked/`ref` access with its behaviour tests still green; conversions that regress benchmarks are reverted or justified. Proof: benchmark table in PR.

**Wave 4**

- C22. Docs deliverables of §4-wave-4 all land; every premise that named DefaultEcs is rewritten or removed **in the same PR**; CHANGELOG Breaking entry with `*Migration:*` per break; `docs/ecs-migration.md` exists.
- C23. #117 closed with outcome; upstream note posted (D8, after user approval).

## 6. Precondition diff (DefaultEcs semantics → facade guarantees)

| Dimension | DefaultEcs today | Facade guarantee (post-migration) | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Set<T>(v)` | add-or-update | add-or-update (never Arch's update-only) | C4, C5/C14 guard |
| Structural change mid-iteration | tolerated (sparse sets) | tolerated (snapshot iteration) | C4 |
| Query membership | maintained sets, predicate re-eval on publish | identical, facade-fired | C4, C11 |
| Changed event payload | `(entity, old, new)`; NotifyChanged ⇒ old==new | identical | C4, C10 |
| World components | native Get/Has/Set/Remove + notifications | singleton entity per world, same API + notifications; Set-when-present ⇒ Changed | C4, C10, M5 tests |
| Iteration order | sparse-set/insertion-ish (undocumented) | **unspecified**; systems needing order sort explicitly | C7/C15 screenshot equivalence + premise |
| `IsAlive` | version-checked handle | same observable semantics via world lookup | C13 |
| Message bus | typed + `[Subscribe]` scan | identical, facade-owned, per-world | C4, compile of 17 handler files |
| `ReadAllComponents` | generic `OnRead<T>` callback | same port, type-registry/reflection-backed, AOT-safe | C4 + `ComponentInspectorTests` |
| Process statics | untracked (bit #117) | every facade/Arch static in `ProcessWideState` | C12 |

## 7. Verification protocol (issue §7, corrected)

```bash
dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj --configuration Release          # core first (MGCB rule)
dotnet test monodreams.sln --configuration Release -m:1 -p:RestoreDisableParallel=true   # ×5 on wave-close
MONODREAMS_TEST_SEED=8 dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/MonoDreams.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --no-build -m:1 -p:RestoreDisableParallel=true
for s in camera physics dialogue ui audio launcher; do dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Demos -- --headless --screen $s --frames 600; done   # --exit is a no-op; --frames drives exit
dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples.Web/MonoDreams.Examples.Web.csproj -p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web
MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT=png MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT_TARGET=Main MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR=<dir> …   # fixed-resolution evidence
```
Plus: pointer-replay scenario against `LevelSelectionScreen` + ui demo, PNG-diffed against a `main` baseline captured the same way — differences explained, never re-baselined. Before every commit: `git grep -l '<<<<<<< HEAD' -- '*.cs' '*.md' '*.json'`; never stage `.worktrees/`.

## 8. Rollback

One PR per wave (D5). Wave 2 is the risky one and touches almost nothing outside `MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/`; reverting it restores DefaultEcs under an unchanged facade. Waves are never squashed together.

content.content: Launching skill: deep-plan

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/.claude/skills/deep-plan

`deep-plan` is `deep-review` run **before** code exists. Where deep-review takes a *diff* and emits *findings*, deep-plan takes a *design intent* (plan-mode prose) + the *live codebase* and emits a **filled, refuted plan-contract** — the four artifacts in the repo's plan-contract spec (`docs/agents/skills-config.md` › Docs layout › Planning; default `docs/planning/plan-contract.md`): Contract block, Interaction matrix, dimension table, Precondition diff — with every matrix cell answered, every derived quantity's base tagged, and every guard copy diffed. That artifact is exactly what `/verify-plan` later reconciles the implementation against.

**Why it exists.** The review side is industrial (lenses + consolidator + facet enumeration). The planning side was a single pass — so the matrix ships with the columns the planner remembered and empty cells, the dimension table with the variables they happened to name, the precondition diff covering the one guard copy they recalled. The same bug class — a deferred/RESERVED record invisible downstream — shipped twice and still needed many review rounds the second time: the missing piece is institutional learning at plan time, not another reviewer. deep-plan points the same specialists that catch these bugs in a diff at the *plan*.

Invocation:

- `/deep-plan` — use the current plan-mode draft (the prose in this session) as the design intent.
- `/deep-plan path/to/draft.md` — read the design intent from a file.
- Append `cheaper` (aliases: `cheap`, `simple`, `eco`, `economy`) for tiered model routing. Default is all-Opus.

This skill reads the repo's `docs/agents/skills-config.md` for everything stack-specific (where docs live, which domains are sensitive, lenses, conventions). When a section is absent it falls back to a stated default and says so in its output.

---

## Model Routing

**Default (full):** all phases and agents use **Opus** with extended thinking.

**Economy mode** (`cheaper`/`cheap`/`simple`/`eco`/`economy`) — mirrors deep-review's tiers, since the agents are the same specialists reframed:

| Phase / Agent | Model | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Agent 1 — Dimension Table | **Opus** (extended thinking) | Deep multi-stage reasoning; base/cap correctness |
| Agent 2 — Caller-Enumerated Matrix Columns | **Sonnet** (extended thinking) | Structured grep + enumerate pattern |
| Agent 3 — State-Mutation Seams | **Opus** (extended thinking) | Complex multi-path mutation logic |
| Agent 4 — Matrix Cells / Lifecycle | **Sonnet** (extended thinking) | Sequential lifecycle against an explicit checklist |
| Agent 5 — Failing-First Tests & Premises | **Sonnet** | Semi-structured obligation analysis |
| Agent 6 — Refuter | **Opus** (extended thinking) | Adversarial; independence is the whole value |

Consolidation (Phase 6) and the Gate always use **Opus** regardless of mode.

---

## Phase 0: Scope tiering

Parse arguments for the **model tier** (detect and strip `cheaper`/etc.). Then classify the change — this decides whether deep-plan fans out at all.

Read the repo's **Sensitive domains** (`docs/agents/skills-config.md` › Sensitive domains). A change touching ANY of them is the bug-prone class this skill exists for. **If none are listed, treat no domain as sensitive — take the light path and never block** (and say so in the output).

**The self-critique paradox: do not over-critique easy tasks.** A heavy enumerate→refute→gate loop on a one-line config tweak is noise that teaches the user to ignore the skill. Tier honestly.

Classify the design intent:

- **TRIVIAL / NON-SENSITIVE** → **light inline pass.** The intent does not touch a Sensitive domain, or touches one only cosmetically (rename, doc, dependency bump, a single non-stateful field). No fan-out. Do Phase 1 context-gathering yourself, then fill the artifacts the change actually needs (often just the Contract block) inline, in one pass. Note explicitly: "Light pass — no sensitive-domain lifecycle change detected." (When the config lists no Sensitive domains at all, every plan takes this path — say "Light pass — no Sensitive domains configured.")

- **SENSITIVE-DOMAIN + STATE/LIFECYCLE/FLOW-REPLACEMENT** → **heavy pass (Workflow).** The intent touches a Sensitive domain (config › Sensitive domains) **and** adds/modifies an entity status or lifecycle, introduces a state machine, or replaces an existing flow/method. Run the deterministic Workflow `.claude/workflows/deep-plan.js` via the Workflow tool (Phases 2–6 below execute inside it). **Always pass `args: { intent, domains, repoRoot }`** where `repoRoot` is the current worktree root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) — agents scope every search to it, and resolve their role files as `${repoRoot}/.claude/skills/deep-plan/agents/…`. (Pass a normal object: the runtime delivers Workflow `args` as a JSON-encoded *string*, and `deep-plan.js` defensively `JSON.parse`s it, so no wrapper is needed — an un-parsed string silently zeroes the intent and runs the whole pass on a blank brief.) **Preflight first** (see Concurrency below): quarantine stale planning artifacts so no agent anchors on another run's file.

When genuinely unsure between tiers, prefer the heavy pass for sensitive domains and say why — a false-heavy is cheap; a false-light ships the gap.

---

## Phase 1: Context gathering (both tiers)

Gather and pass to every agent (read paths from `docs/agents/skills-config.md` › Docs layout, substituting `{domain}`/`{module}` per the configured premises pattern; if a path is absent, default to `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` + `docs/{domain}/premises.md` and say so):

1. **The design intent** — the plan-mode prose (or the intent file). This is the analogue of deep-review's diff: the source of truth for *what is being proposed*. There is no diff; the codebase on disk is the *current* (pre-change) state.
2. **The recurring-failure-modes doc** (config › Docs layout › Planning) — **mandatory when present.** Every entry whose trigger matches the change is a question the plan must answer. This is the mechanism that makes a new plan consult past lessons. If the repo has no such doc, note its absence and rely on the core tenets + premises.
3. **The core-tenets doc** (config › Docs layout › Core tenets; default `docs/CORE_TENETS.md`) — invariants every agent checks the intent against.
4. **Affected domains** — detect each changed/affected file's domain via **Domains** (config › Domains — path-glob → domain). For each, read its schema doc and premises (config › Docs layout).
5. **Touched flows** — from the flows dir (config › Flows, default `docs/flows/`), read the flow doc of every flow the intent touches (frontmatter `covers:` globs). A flow doc is the dedicated core-tenet for that flow — its invariants and load-bearing quantities are exactly what the dimension table and lifecycle matrix must hold the change to.
5. **The plan-contract spec** (config › Docs layout › Planning; default `docs/planning/plan-contract.md`) — the artifact spec the output must conform to.
6. **The repo conventions** — `docs/agents/skills-config.md` itself plus any rules dir it points at (config › Docs layout › rules dir).

**Pass to all agents:** the design intent, the recurring-failure-modes doc, the core-tenets doc, relevant schema + premises docs, the touched flow docs, the plan-contract spec, the affected-domain list. Agents have full file tools (Read, Grep, Bash) and **must use them** — unlike deep-review, the codebase is the *current* state, so an agent's job is to discover, in real code, the callers/guards/readers the intent will collide with.

---

## Phase 2: ENUMERATE (heavy pass)

Before analysis, build the real enumeration the plan-contract needs — this is what a single planning pass skips. Two sweeps (Agent 2 owns the first, Agent 3/Agent 1 feed the second):

- **Interaction-matrix columns.** Grep every site that reads or transitions the state the new record touches (the membership collection it feeds, the central create/transition method, status-from-children rollups, `findByStatus`, exhaustive `when(status)`/`switch`/`match` blocks, status-membership helpers). Each distinct reader becomes a **column**. A generic adjacent-event list is the floor, not the column set — see the plan-contract spec Artifact 2.
- **Guard copies.** For every guard/gate/predicate the intent tightens or copies, grep **all** copies across the codebase. Each copy becomes a precondition-diff row.

Output of this phase is the *column set* and the *copy set* — concrete, codebase-derived, feeding Phases 3–4.

## Phase 3: ANALYZE (heavy pass)

Launch the specialists. Each reads its role file under `.claude/skills/deep-plan/agents/` and produces a **structured contract slice**, not prose findings:

| Agent | Role file | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Dimension Table | `agents/dimension-table.md` | Artifact 4: variable→unit/base→cap→seam (money is the canonical kind; any load-bearing derived value qualifies) |
| 2 — Caller-Enumerated Matrix Columns | `agents/matrix-columns.md` | Artifact 2 *columns* (the enumeration) |
| 3 — State-Mutation Seams | `agents/state-mutation-seams.md` | every state-creation/mutation seam + the `require`/`check` each needs |
| 4 — Matrix Cells / Lifecycle | `agents/lifecycle-matrix.md` | Artifact 2 *cells*: `handled`/`N/A`/`GAP` per (state × event) |
| 5 — Failing-First Tests & Premises | `agents/test-coverage.md` | failing-first test obligations + executable-premise proposals + premise/doc drift |
| 6 — Refuter | `agents/refuter.md` | (Phase 4 — runs against the draft only) |

Agents 1 and 3 carry the **flow-specific concern** — they read the repo's **flow docs** (config › Flows) for the invariants this repo's key flows depend on and hold the change to them. The backend's flows (e.g. a `payment-pipeline` doc tagging every value's base/cap; a `dsa-lifecycle` doc listing a new status × every adjacent entity event) are the *example* of what the flow docs contain; your repo's are whatever it declares.

## Phase 4: REFUTE (heavy pass) — loop-until-dry

Agent 6 (the refuter) gets **only the draft contract**, not the reasoning that produced it — anchoring-free. Its job: find one unhandled scenario, one dimension/cap violation, or one wrongly-`handled` cell. Refute-or-promote. Each refutation carries an **`attacks` tag** — `resolution` (it breaks a fill/fix the draft already contains) vs `new-surface` (it names territory the draft lacks) — which the verdict aggregates per round to tell fix-attack equilibrium apart from undiscovered surface. The Workflow runs **`REFUTERS_PER_ROUND` refuters in parallel per round** (each assigned a **distinct attack lens** — quantity/dimensional · async-ordering/lifecycle · premise/invariant · completeness/wrong-cell — plus the list of already-open roots, so the N refuters cover N near-independent surfaces instead of colliding on the same targets or re-raising a known GAP), and loops until **2 consecutive rounds surface nothing new** or it hits `MAX_REFUTE_ROUNDS`; each surfaced gap reopens the relevant cell/row and forces Phase 3's owner to resolve it. Independence is the point — it breaks the cascade where planner and reviewer share a blind spot.

**Resolution re-refute (when the loop ends at the round cap).** Ending at `MAX_REFUTE_ROUNDS` right after a resolve means the **final resolver patch was never attacked** — every earlier patch was re-attacked by the next round, but the last one ships unexamined. The Workflow runs **one targeted pass** (`RESOLUTION_REREFUTERS`, default 2, `ARGS.reRefuters` overrides) scoped to ONLY those final resolutions — not a full re-sweep — and integrates any break with a single resolver call. The regress ends there by design: the verdict reports the outcome ("all held" is a real signal; "N fresh, integrated" means the re-refute's own patch ships unattacked — weigh it accordingly, and reach for an independent re-run if it matters).

## Phase 5: GATE (heavy pass) — programmatic completeness

The Workflow's `Gate` phase flags any of:

- an interaction-matrix cell that is **empty or `GAP` without written justification**;
- a load-bearing premise (correctness-critical) with **no `require`/`check` seam or no failing-first test**;
- a touched guard with **no per-copy precondition diff**.

It runs a **bounded justify loop** (`GATE_JUSTIFY_ROUNDS`): each pass is fed the gate violations *plus* the deterministic missing-cell list (`missingCells`), so when a refuter grew the matrix with a new column/state the justify pass fills the **whole** new row/column, not just the cell the refuter named. After the loop, any residual GAP is **recorded in the result (`gate: FAIL`, `residualGaps`, `violations`) and surfaced at the top of the body — never thrown.** deep-plan never blocks (Phase 7): a throw here once lost ~3M tokens / 2h on 91 empty cells a single justify pass left after matrix growth, *before synthesize ever ran*. A flagged contract is incomparably more useful than a 0-byte output. (Seed mode keeps its own throw for the gate-detects-incompleteness test.)

## Phase 6: SYNTHESIZE (heavy pass)

The contract is rendered **deterministically in JS from the gated draft**, not retyped by an LLM. `renderVerdict()` builds the verdict header — a count of any **`### ⚠️ Contradiction`** themes the consolidator flagged (surfaced FIRST — the gate checks completeness, not *consistency* between two commitments, so a contract that says "source X from A" beside "source X from B" passes the gate; this leads with it); the substantive-GAP count plus its **clustering** into distinct code seams + the Síntese decision-theme count (so the headline reads ~decisions, not ~cells — most cells are one un-built surface repeated across rows); the refute-convergence status with the **per-round trajectory shape** (`[11, 11, 8]` → FLAT = surface far from exhausted, re-run; `[11, 5, 1]` → DECAYING = a round or two more would close it) plus the **final-round mix** of resolution-attacks vs new-surface (a FLAT shape with a high resolution share means the loop is *generative* — each resolver patch mints new attack surface — not that the original surface is unexplored) and the **resolution re-refute outcome**; the reframed gate verdict; and a `### ⚠️ Unresolved` list of every GAP cell + unresolved dimension violation. `renderArtifacts()` renders the four artifacts (Contract block + Interaction matrix + dimension table + Precondition diff + premises) **losslessly** — every draft row appears verbatim, with no output-token ceiling. The consolidator (`agents/consolidate.md`) writes **only** the narrative synthesis (`## Síntese` — clustering the GAPs/refutations into the BLOCKERs the planner must decide), sandwiched between the header and the artifacts. Retyping the artifacts through the LLM is exactly what dropped 16 of 70 contract items on a real run (the recurring consolidation-lossiness class); moving the render to JS removes that lossy step entirely.

**The state axis is canonicalized before render** (`canonicalizeMatrixStates`, applied inside every `applyPatch`): a downstream fill/refute/justify agent paraphrases an enumerated state into a terser convention ("status=STOPLOSS" vs the verbose "StoreStopLoss.status = STOPLOSS (…)"), which `normCode`'s full-label fallback can't collapse — so on a real run the matrix DOUBLED to 18 states / 576 cells (9 / 288 real), the gate-justify pass filled ~288 phantom cells, and the GAP count read 2× the truth. The canonicalizer collapses verbose/terse variants of the same logical state (suffix-anchored loose key), remaps the cells, and merges collisions (GAP wins, so a merge never hides open work).

**Three programmatic checks** still run over the rendered body — but as a **regression guard on the engine's render**, not a cure for LLM-retype lossiness (which is now gone): (1) `consolidationFidelity()` (DROP class — anchor absent everywhere), (2) `contractBlockCoverage()` (BURIED class — a commitment outside the numbered `## Contract` block; it anchors on the heading whose text *begins* with "contract", not the document title `## deep-plan contract — …`), (3) `structuralCounts()` (SHORTFALL class — a collection rendering *fewer* rows than the draft holds). With deterministic render these are always clean; a hit means `renderArtifacts` itself dropped something (an engine bug), so it is **logged + surfaced in the result, never patched by an LLM repair pass.** The narrative is `stripPreamble`-trimmed to its first heading (a model can leak task narration before it). Residuals are reported in the run result (`consolidationOmissions`, `contractBuried`, `contractBlockMissing`, `structuralCounts`, `structuralShortfalls`).

---

## Phase 7: Verdict (advisory-loud) and next step

deep-plan **never blocks** plan finalization — plan mode is used for one-liners too, and a hard gate there needs a fragile escape hatch. Instead it surfaces residual gaps prominently, then asks what to do with `AskUserQuestion`.

The **heavy (Workflow) pass already emits its own verdict header** — `## deep-plan contract — …` followed by a `### Verdict` block (contradiction count if any, substantive-GAP count + clustering, refute-convergence status + per-round trajectory shape + final-round resolution/new-surface mix + resolution re-refute outcome, reframed gate verdict) and a `### ⚠️ Unresolved` list, all rendered by `renderVerdict()`. Present that body as-is; you only add a one-line **Mode·Tier** banner above it (metadata the Workflow can't know):

```markdown
**Mode**: {Full Opus | Economy (tiered)} · **Tier**: Heavy (Workflow)
```

For a **light inline pass** (no Workflow), prepend the full header yourself:

```markdown
## deep-plan: {plan name or intent summary}

**Mode**: {Full Opus | Economy (tiered)} · **Tier**: Light inline
**Affected domains**: {list}
**Residual GAPs**: {count — 0 means the contract is complete}
```

If there are residual GAPs, list them first, each as `⚠️ GAP: <state> × <event/variable> — <why unresolved>`.

Then `AskUserQuestion` — options:

1. **Write artifacts into the plan** — append the filled Contract / Matrix / Dimension table / Precondition diff to the plan file (or the in-session plan draft), replacing any hand-filled versions. When committing a standalone contract, write it to **`.claude/deep-plan/<branch>-<shortSha>.md`** (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD`) — branch+commit makes it unique per run and is exactly what the PR-gate reads.
2. **Save gap report to file** — write to a **run-unique** path `.claude/deep-plan/<branch>-<shortSha>/report.md` (or the repo's own scratch dir — never a shared `/tmp/deep-plan-{name}.md`; a flat name in a shared temp dir is the contamination vector that wrecked a real run).
3. **Proceed anyway** — leave the plan as-is; the GAPs are recorded in the conversation. (Used when a GAP is a deliberate, justified exclusion.)
4. **Nothing** — keep it in the conversation output.

The real choke point is downstream: the `gh pr create` PreToolUse hook (the repo's PR-gate, installed under `.claude/`) blocks sensitive-domain branches whose plan-contract is incomplete or whose `/verify-plan` is not clean. deep-plan at plan time is advisory; the hook at PR time is the gate.

---

## Key rules

- **Enumerate from the codebase, never from memory.** The single defining difference from a one-pass planner: matrix columns and guard copies are *grepped*, not recalled. A column set that matches your memory is suspect — grep anyway.
- **The intent is the source of truth for what is proposed; the codebase is the current state.** When the intent contradicts what the code can support, that contradiction is a finding, not something to silently reconcile.
- **The dimension axis is king.** A load-bearing derived value with no tagged base or no cap seam is a Blocker-class gap, exactly as in deep-review. Money is the canonical case; a count, a window-bounded sum, or a ratio with the wrong base is the same bug.
- **Refute independently.** The refuter must not see the analysis reasoning — only the draft contract. Sharing context defeats it.
- **Tier honestly (self-critique paradox).** Don't fan out on trivial or non-sensitive plans; don't light-pass a sensitive-domain lifecycle change.

---

## Concurrency, contamination & search hygiene

These are not optional polish — each maps to an observed failure when running deep-plan across multiple worktrees.

- **Scope every search to the repo root with `rg`, never `grep -r`.** `rg` honors `.gitignore`, so it skips build output, the VCS dir, and **worktrees** — a bare `grep -r` from a worktree traverses build artifacts and every sibling worktree and has hung a run for **87 minutes**. This applies to the light inline pass too. Never read or search `/tmp`, `..`, `~`, or absolute paths outside the current repo. Keep each Bash call one simple command (a fragile `rg … | head; echo; find …` one-liner hangs on an unbalanced quote). Bound any DB/MCP query (`LIMIT`).

- **Contamination guard.** Running multiple deep-plans concurrently, an agent that searches broadly can read **another run's** artifact (a stale `deep-plan-*.md`, a sibling worktree's plan-contract) and silently re-anchor the whole contract to the wrong feature (observed: an "apuração" plan came back 100% about "retention-bonus"). The workflow's `ctx()` injects a guard telling agents the inline intent is the only source of truth — reinforce it in the intent text when two live branches touch the same domain: *"this change is X, NOT Y; ignore any artifact mentioning Y."*

- **Preflight quarantine.** Before a heavy run, move stale flat artifacts out of the search path: `mkdir -p ~/.deepplan-quarantine && mv /tmp/deep-plan-*.md ~/.deepplan-quarantine/ 2>/dev/null || true`. With `rg`-scoping this is belt-and-suspenders, but it's cheap insurance.

- **Run-unique outputs.** Key any saved artifact by branch + short SHA (Phase 7) — `<branch>-<shortSha>` is unique per worktree+commit; append `-<unixTimestamp>` if you keep multiple runs on the same commit. (The org/repo is already encoded by the repo path.) A flat shared-temp name re-contaminates the next run. Note: unique *naming* alone is insufficient — the real fix is that agents no longer read shared temp or sibling worktrees at all (`rg`-scoping above); a uniquely-named stale file is still found by an unscoped `grep`.

- **Matrix axis↔cell integrity: every (state,column) is keyed by its leading CODE (`normCode`), not its full label.** The matrix had a latent bug that only surfaced at scale: refuters/resolvers write cells under drifting label variants — `"S1"` vs `"S1 PERFORMANCE_BONUS_RETAINED"`, `"C1"` vs `"C1 RETENTION mint hook"` — and the gate keyed by exact string. A 4-refuter × 5-round run wrote cells under 68 column-labels (→ 34 codes) and 22 state-labels (→ 15 codes), so the gate saw **374 phantom-empty grid pairs** and a single 59k justify pass re-created 374 duplicates while the real analysis sat in 105 orphaned cells. The fix: `gateCheck` and `applyPatch` key cells by `normCode`, and `applyPatch` reconciles any cell's state/column code back into the axes — so the gate validates the *real* analyzed surface, label variants collapse, and the `refKey` dedup/dry-streak can finally fire. **The gate-violation count tracks refuter invocations under the bug (6→1, 6→84, 20→374); fix the data structure, don't cap the loop.**
- **Refute breadth and depth: 4 lensed refuters/round (`REFUTERS_PER_ROUND`, `ARGS.refutersPerRound` overrides), capped at 3 rounds (`MAX_REFUTE_ROUNDS`), early-exit after 2 dry rounds (`DRY_ROUNDS_TO_STOP`).** History: a 4×5 run *did* reach the full r1+r2 cluster union in one run, but at ~1.8× cost, still no convergence (flat 16/12/15/15/15), and the 374-violation gate above — because more refuters *amplified* the then-unfixed label drift. Once that amplifier was fixed twice over (`normCode` keying + `canonicalizeMatrixStates`) and a coherent matrix was confirmed, breadth was **re-raised deliberately 2→4** — the post-mortem's own invitation. The lever is *breadth, not depth*: the FLAT `11/11/8` trajectory showed coverage-per-round (the number of distinct attack angles) was the binding constraint, and refuters run in **parallel** so breadth is ~free on wall-clock (it trades tokens for coverage); raising *rounds* (depth) just burns serial wall-clock without converging. To keep added refuters from colliding, each takes a **distinct lens** (quantity/dimension · async-ordering · premise · completeness). The ceiling is the resolver patch size (all fresh funnel into ONE patch → StructuredOutput bloat), not thinking — so it is a band, not "more is better". Each round still feeds refuters the **already-open roots** (GAP cells + unresolved violations) so they push to new territory. For *coverage* still prefer an independent re-run over raising rounds — see **One run does not exhaust** below.

- **Terseness prevents crashes.** Oversized drafts make the resolver/consolidator's `StructuredOutput` call return nothing and waste the run (~600 KB observed). The schemas cap verbose fields and the prompts demand `file:line + one clause`. Don't relax that.

- **The iterative resolver returns a PATCH, not the whole draft.** Re-emitting the full — and growing — draft every refute/gate round is what hit the 64k output-token ceiling: on a real run the round-5 refuter found its *strongest* refutation (a creation-time amortization gap) and the resolver then returned nothing, silently dropping it. The refute-resolve and gate-justify steps now emit only the cells/rows/premises/columns they add or change (`DRAFT_PATCH`), which `applyPatch()` merges by key. The merge is additive/override-only, so a thin or malformed patch degrades to "gate still fails", never to silent corruption. The initial **fill** is now a PATCH too (Lever 1): the matrix specialist (Agent 4) already answers every cell into the draft, so the fill no longer re-emits the matrix — it returns only the precondition rows, the Contract block, and any cells the deterministic `missingCells` check still reports missing. Re-emitting all ~N cells was the run's long pole (~35 min on a 28×14 matrix) and itself risked the StructuredOutput crash; cartesian completeness is enforced by the gate's justify loop, not by costly re-emission. `applyPatch` + `gateCheck` + `missingCells` are exercised deterministically via the script's `seedPatch` / `seedDraft` / `seedMissing` test modes.

---

## One run does not exhaust — the multi-run protocol

A single heavy pass samples a *fraction* of the finding space, and the refute loop reaching `MAX_REFUTE_ROUNDS` is **not** a signal it found everything. The evidence across four dogfood runs of the *same* plan: r1 and r2 agreed on only ~4 core clusters while each caught 4–6 the other missed; r3 at 4×5 reached the r1+r2 union but never went dry (flat 16/12/15/15/15); r4 at half r3's budget (18 agents, ~3.1M tokens) **still surfaced 6 new confirmed premises including a blocker**. The variance lives in the refuter's *attack-angle sampling*, not in loop depth — so cranking `MAX_REFUTE_ROUNDS` buys little; an *independent* re-run buys a lot.

For a high-stakes sensitive-domain plan, **run deep-plan 2+ times and union the findings**, rather than trusting one deep pass:

1. Each run already writes a run-unique deliverable `.claude/deep-plan/<branch>-<shortSha>.md` (add `-<timestamp>` for same-commit re-runs). Keep them side by side.
2. **Union, don't intersect:** a finding present in *any* run is in scope. Reconcile the Contract blocks, the matrix `GAP` cells, and the premises across runs; a commitment in run B but not run A is a real gap run A missed, not noise.
3. **Strike revoked items — never append a revision beside the commitment it supersedes.** When a later run *overturns* an earlier decision, the union must delete or visibly strike the superseded item, not carry both. A real run opened with **7 contradictions — all 7** were a stale unioned commitment sitting beside the revision that replaced it: union debt, not new findings.
4. **Scan the unioned document for contradictions at reconciliation time** — two commitments giving conflicting directives for the same mechanism/seam, the same check the consolidator runs in-run. The gate never catches these (completeness, not consistency), so the hand-reconciliation is the only place this happens between runs.
5. **The first run fed with the unioned contract is the designated re-refute of the union** — not an optional extra. Contradictions it flags are the *expected output* of union debt; they render first in the verdict — resolve them before reading any other finding.
6. Treat a run that surfaces *zero* new load-bearing findings as the real convergence signal — two such runs in a row is "dry" at the run level, the analogue of the in-run dry-streak. A cheaper leading indicator: when a run spends more of its top findings *revoking* earlier decisions than discovering new surface, the design is near its fixpoint even while the in-run refute trajectory stays FLAT.

This is breadth at the *run* level: cheaper and higher-yield than raising **round depth** (`MAX_REFUTE_ROUNDS`), which the FLAT trajectory shows never converges. Per-round **breadth** (`REFUTERS_PER_ROUND`, now 4 lensed) is the one in-run knob worth raising — it adds near-independent attack surfaces per round at ~no wall-clock cost — and `ARGS.refutersPerRound` dials it per-run for an unusually large change. But for *coverage* of the finding space, an independent re-run still beats raising any in-run knob; reach for it first, and read the new run's `### Verdict` trajectory shape to decide whether another is warranted.

**Branch sugerida:** `issue-119-wave0` → `issue-119-wave1` → `issue-119-wave2` → `issue-119-wave3` → `issue-119-wave4` — five stacked branches, one PR per wave (issue §10: "Each wave is its own PR. Do not squash waves together.").

DefaultEcs (pinned 0.18.0-beta01) is unmaintained and carries a live correctness bug (#117: EntityQueryFilterFactory cache-key collision; #118 landed a workaround). The decision (issue #119): ship (1) MonoDreams.Ecs, an engine-owned facade in MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ (namespace MonoDreams.Ecs) that becomes the ONLY ECS surface for every other module, Examples, Demos, CLI-scaffolded games and tests; then (2) swap the facade's backend from DefaultEcs to Arch (https://github.com/genaray/Arch). Behaviour preserved; only ECS plumbing moves. Non-goals: gameplay/module logic rewrites, component-shape changes, Arch.Relationships/Persistence, renderer changes. Read issue #119 §1–§5 (gh issue view 119) for the full measured API-usage table and hazards H1–H10.

Key hazards from the issue: H1 Set semantics invert (DefaultEcs Set = add-or-update; Arch Set = update-only, Add = add-only; 1826 call sites); H2 structural changes during iteration unsafe in Arch (archetype moves); H3 no persistent EntitySet in Arch; H4 iteration order changes (sparse-set → archetype/chunk); H5 no world components in Arch; H6 entity handle lifetime/IsAlive; H7 Arch's reactive events are compiled out of the published NuGet (#if EVENTS) — silent no-op; H8 managed (class) components land in object arrays; H9 Arch keeps static World.Worlds registry + component-type statics (same shape as the #117/#118 flake); H10 world construction args differ entirely.

**Domínios:** foundation (sensitive), all 14 modules, examples, cli, platform, tests
**Tier de risco:** deep-plan — engine-wide flow replacement crossing all 14 modules, rooted in sensitive foundation.

## 1. Context

DefaultEcs (pinned 0.18.0-beta01) is unmaintained and carries a live correctness bug (#117: EntityQueryFilterFactory cache-key collision; #118 landed a workaround). The decision (issue #119): ship (1) MonoDreams.Ecs, an engine-owned facade in MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ (namespace MonoDreams.Ecs) that becomes the ONLY ECS surface for every other module, Examples, Demos, CLI-scaffolded games and tests; then (2) swap the facade's backend from DefaultEcs to Arch (https://github.com/genaray/Arch). Behaviour preserved; only ECS plumbing moves. Non-goals: gameplay/module logic rewrites, component-shape changes, Arch.Relationships/Persistence, renderer changes. Read issue #119 §1–§5 (gh issue view 119 --repo roo-oliv/monodreams) for the full measured API-usage table and hazards H1–H10.

Key hazards from the issue: H1 Set semantics invert (DefaultEcs Set = add-or-update; Arch Set = update-only, Add = add-only; 1826 call sites); H2 structural changes during iteration unsafe in Arch (archetype moves); H3 no persistent EntitySet in Arch; H4 iteration order changes (sparse-set → archetype/chunk); H5 no world components in Arch; H6 entity handle lifetime/IsAlive; H7 Arch's reactive events are compiled out of the published NuGet (#if EVENTS) — silent no-op; H8 managed (class) components land in object arrays; H9 Arch keeps static World.Worlds registry + component-type statics (same shape as the #117/#118 flake); H10 world construction args differ entirely.

## 2. Verification deltas (measured on main @ 7b2cbe2a, 2026-08-18)

### 2a. Surfaces the issue's table MISSES (each needs a facade shape)

- M1 Value-predicate queries `.With((in T c) => …)` — 2 sites: MonoDreams/physics/System/GravitySystem.cs:10, MonoDreams/rendering/System/Draw/MasterRenderSystem.cs:90 (BuildDrawSet). Arch has NO value-predicate filter. Documented engine premise (foundation — "A value-predicate EntitySet re-evaluates only when the component is published"): predicate runs only on publication (Set/NotifyChanged), cached as membership. Facade must own publication-driven predicate membership — highest-risk item.
- M2 entity.NotifyChanged<T>() — ~40 sites across cursor, ui, debug, level-editor, tests. The engine's publication verb: re-runs predicate sets AND fires Changed subscriptions with old == new (AudioSystem relies on ReferenceEquals(old,new) — AudioSystem.cs:141). Facade must own it.
- M3 [Subscribe] attribute + world.Subscribe(this) — 17 [Subscribe] handlers across 14 files; 9 Subscribe(this) sites (plus 19 typed Subscribe<T> sites). Facade message bus must support BOTH registration forms, AOT-safe.
- M4 ParallelSystem<T> — 5 uses, all in MonoDreams/level-editor/Composition/EditorPipelineRegistrar.cs. All hosts create DefaultParallelRunner(1) — degree 1 — so a sequential implementation behind the same name is behaviour-preserving.
- M5 World components: 4 types, not 2, and world-level Remove<T>() — LDtkLevelDataComponent, EntityHierarchy, CurrentLevelComponent, CurrentBackgroundColorComponent; 6 world-Remove sites (LDtkLevelLoadSystem.cs:71,80,81; EditorTransport.cs:399,400,411,412). Facade singleton store needs Set/Get/Has/Remove + Added/Removed/Changed notifications. Restart transport semantics (Set over present component fires Changed not Added — CORE_TENETS §9) preserved exactly.
- M6 SubscribeEntityComponentChanged handler carries (in Entity, in T old, in T new) — BoundaryBakeSystem.cs:97, AudioSystem.cs:42, TileGridBakeSystem.cs:159. Arch's Set events do NOT deliver the old value → facade-fired events are the only viable design (D1).
- M7 IGameScreen exposes ISystem<GameState> (MonoDreams/foundation/Screen/GameScreen.cs:11-13); 71 engine files reference ISystem<GameState>. The public screen contract itself moves to the facade's ISystem<T>.
- M8 ReadAllComponents: 3 sites (+ MonoDreams.Examples.Core/Inspector/ComponentIntrospector.cs:9,39) via IComponentReader with generic OnRead<T> callback.
- M9 Packaging: 4 csproj (MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj:143, MonoDreams.Examples.Core:38, MonoDreams.Demos:25, scratchpad/blazor-spike/MonoDreams.Spike:58 — git-tracked, out of sln) + MonoDreams/packages.lock.json:11 + MonoDreams/module.schema.json:55 doc example + MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj:31-33 comment.
- M10 Reactive callback doing structural mutation inside the publish path — TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.cs:89,94 — entity.Set<ColliderTagComponent>() from inside a ComponentAdded handler; subscription IDisposables discarded (:74-75). Hardest case under an archetype backend.
- M11 MonoDreams.Cli module registry + scaffolded games must emit facade usings/packages; manifest-honesty CI proves per module.

### 2b. Corrections DOWNWARD

- SystemProfiler needs zero migration (static class feeding GatedSystem.TimingSink; no DefaultEcs reference).
- ISuspendableSystem has no DefaultEcs coupling (one cast site GatedSystem.cs:130).
- EntityQuery.Count NOT required (the apparent .Count hit is a HashSet<Entity>). Required surface: construct-once, With<T>/Without<T>/value-predicate, GetEntities() snapshot enumeration valid within the frame, first-match-and-break, transient using-disposable queries, Dispose().
- DrawPrepSystemBase is dead code — zero subclasses, its useParallel param actually maps to DefaultEcs useBuffer. Delete in wave 1.
- Structural-mutation surface: 3 unsafe engine AEntitySetSystem sites (CullingSystem.cs:100,107; ButtonMeshPrepSystem.cs:83; TextPrepSystem.cs:75) + GameOverSystem (Examples; creates AND disposes mid-iteration) + ~6 unsafe manual-iteration sites (SelectionSystem.cs:404-415 +4 more, TabSystem.cs:71-77, DialogSystem.cs:38-51, TileGridPaintSystem.cs:162, HudPreviewSystem.cs:74) + the M10 callback. ~7 editor systems already buffer-then-mutate.
- ScreenController RECEIVES an IParallelRunner (ctor param, re-exposed as Runner); hosts create DefaultParallelRunner(1). 9 system types across 5 files consume a runner.
- Demos has 6 screens (camera, physics, dialogue, ui, audio, launcher); --exit is a no-op (exit driven by --frames). Solution file is lowercase monodreams.sln. No benchmark project exists.

### 2c. Repo facts

- Commits/PRs in English, Conventional Commits; branch naming issue-<N>. Core builds before heads (MGCB absolute-path rule).
- Guard-test model: MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/EditorThemeLintTests.cs (git-tracked source scan, comment-stripping, allowlist) + ManifestHonestyTests KnownGaps ratchet.
- Process-wide state: MonoDreams.Tests/ProcessWideState.cs + ProcessWideStateGuardAttribute + DeterministicCollectionOrderer. No DefaultEcs statics tracked today. Any facade/Arch static must be registered in ProcessWideState in the PR that introduces it (H9).
- CI: ci.yml = xvfb-run dotnet test Release -m:1; manifest-honesty.yml = per-module scaffold+add+build matrix.
- CHANGELOG: ## Unreleased → ### Breaking — <summary> ([#119]) + *Migration:* clauses.
- Premises naming DefaultEcs to rewrite: foundation (preamble :7; :393; :505; value-predicate premise :692 — rewrite entirely), collision (:223 [Subscribe] semantics), audio (:14, :207 version-pinned pub/sub claim; overview :42), rendering (:772 AsSet() lifecycle), level-editor (:1260 composites; :1509 ReadAllComponents; overview :29,:66), ui (:988,:993), dialogue (:222), camera (:235 + overview :30 + docs/flows/camera.md:83 — iteration-order claims are DefaultEcs-specific).
- Env: .NET SDK 8.0.416 with wasm-tools installed.

## 3. Recorded design decisions

- D1 (H7): facade-fired reactive notifications — option (a). Facade owns Set/Add/Remove/Destroy/SetSingleton/NotifyChanged and raises the engine's events itself; Arch's EVENTS-flag events stay off. Mandatory: Changed carries (old,new) (M6), NotifyChanged must fire Changed with old==new (M2), predicate membership (M1) needs a publication hook. Vendoring Arch with EVENTS defined is the documented fallback.
- D2 (H2): EntitySystem<T> iterates a materialized snapshot buffer — structural changes (Set-new/Remove/Dispose/Create) during Update stay safe, matching today. Documented as a facade premise.
- D3 (H3): EntityQuery maintains publication-driven materialized membership (updated by the facade's own add/remove/publish events), enumeration hands out a frame-stable snapshot; transient using queries supported. Count deliberately unimplemented.
- D4: facade keeps DefaultEcs-shaped names — entity.Set (add-or-update), entity.Get<T>() → ref T, Has/Remove, entity.Dispose(), entity.IsAlive (property), world.CreateEntity(), world.Subscribe/Publish, Subscribe(Entity|World)Component*, NotifyChanged — wave 1 dominated by using swaps; the 1826 Set call sites never see Arch's update-only Set (guard-enforced).
- D5: five stacked PRs opened sequentially without waiting for merges; wave N+1's PR base = wave N's branch. (Confirm at approval.)
- D6: Arch.AOT.SourceGenerator yes; Arch.System.SourceGenerator optional wave-3-only if benchmarks justify; Arch.EventBus/Persistence/Relationships/LowLevel no.
- D7: scratchpad/blazor-spike/ deleted in wave 4. (Confirm at approval.)
- D8: after wave 4 merges, comment on Doraku/DefaultEcs#197 and close #117. (Confirm at approval.)

## 4. Waves

Wave 0 — spike & baseline (issue-119-wave0, base main): MonoDreams.Benchmarks (BenchmarkDotNet, in monodreams.sln): creation, structural churn, iteration 10k/100k/1M, struct + managed-DrawComponent-shaped cases, DefaultEcs vs Arch side by side; RESULTS.md committed. Target proofs: Arch under KNI/BlazorGL WASM build; AOT publish (PublishAot=true) smoke with Arch.AOT.SourceGenerator. H7 proof: runnable sample of facade-fired Added/Changed(old,new)/Removed + singleton notifications + predicate membership over Arch, exercising the M10 shape. Findings in PR; plan amended before wave 1 if invalidated.

Wave 1 — facade with DefaultEcs backend (issue-119-wave1): MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ implements MonoDreams.Ecs covering issue §4 + M1–M8, delegating to DefaultEcs: World/Entity aliased, EcsWorld.Create() (H10), EntityQuery (+ predicates), EntitySystem<T> (reads [With]/[Without]), SequentialSystem/ParallelSystem/ActionSystem/AComponentSystem, ISystem<T>, IParallelRunner + default runner, message bus (typed + [Subscribe]), world singletons (4 types + Remove), reactive subscriptions (5 verbs, exact handler signatures), NotifyChanged, ReadAllComponents(IComponentReader). All ~321 files migrate (engine 176, tests 100, Examples.Core 34, Demos 7, heads). Delete DrawPrepSystemBase. IGameScreen moves to facade types. Guard test MonoDreams.Tests/Architecture/EcsBoundaryLintTests.cs (modeled on EditorThemeLintTests + KnownGaps ratchet): no git-tracked .cs outside MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ (and scratchpad/, until deleted) may reference DefaultEcs (from wave 2: nor Arch). New facade premises in foundation/docs/premises.md. Zero behaviour change: full-solution Release gate green ×5; MONODREAMS_TEST_SEED=8 green; headless Demos screenshots byte-identical to main baseline, all 6 screens.

Wave 2 — swap backend to Arch (issue-119-wave2): only MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ + dependency edits. Work H1–H10 + M1/M2/M3/M5/M6/M10 site by site; every facade/Arch static registered in ProcessWideState; hygiene tests extended (H9); tests leaking new World() get disposal. All 11 reactive sites verified working by a test each, incl. M10 mutation-inside-handler and Restart Changed-not-Added (M5). Guard extended: no raw Arch. outside facade. Acceptance: gate ×5 + seeded green; 6/6 demos non-blank + flat heap; Examples boots Level_0 and Blender_Level; .mdscene round-trip; web head builds; pointer-replay PNG diff vs main explained difference-by-difference, never re-baselined (H4). Benchmarks re-run vs wave-0 baseline (H8 managed components measured, NOT converted).

Wave 3 — hot paths (issue-119-wave3): chunk/ref queries for CullingSystem, SpritePrepSystem, TextPrepSystem, MeshPrepSystem, YSortSystem, MasterRenderSystem feed, GravitySystem, VelocitySystem, TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.BuildEntries. Opt-in chunked override on EntitySystem<T>; Arch.System.SourceGenerator only if measurably better. Benchmarks improve or hold; conversions that regress are reverted or justified.

Wave 4 — cleanup & docs (issue-119-wave4): remove DefaultEcs from every csproj/lockfile/module.json; update module.schema.json example; delete scratchpad/blazor-spike/; regenerate locks. monodreams init + add <every module> compiles — manifest-honesty green all legs. Retire #118 DefaultEcs-specific defensive resets where moot; keep seeded harness + hygiene guard. Docs sweep: CORE_TENETS, foundation overview facade tour, all premises naming DefaultEcs, .claude/CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/skills-config.md stack line, README (+credits reworded historically), CONTRIBUTING, docs/web-targeting.md:189, docs/index.md, docs/flows/camera.md:83; new docs/ecs-migration.md; CHANGELOG Breaking entry with *Migration:* lines. Close #117; upstream note on Doraku/DefaultEcs#197.

## 5. Contract (C1–C23)

C1 Benchmarks project runs, RESULTS.md committed. C2 Arch compiles into KNI/BlazorGL WASM + AOT publish. C3 facade-fired event design proven end-to-end over Arch incl. M10 shape and Changed(old,new). C4 MonoDreams.Ecs exposes issue §4 + M1–M8 complete; EcsFacadeContractTests per guarantee (Set add-or-update; NotifyChanged fires Changed old==new; predicate membership updates on publish only; snapshot iteration tolerates Set/Remove/Dispose mid-loop; singleton Set-when-present fires Changed not Added; world Remove fires Removed). C5 zero DefaultEcs outside facade (EcsBoundaryLintTests, ratchet empty). C6 DrawPrepSystemBase deleted. C7 wave-1 behaviour identity: gate ×5, seeded, 6/6 byte-identical PNGs vs main. C8 new foundation premises, each with Tests: named — no new premise ships Tests: none yet. C9 wave-2 diff scoped to facade + manifests. C10 the 11 reactive sites each have a named passing test through the facade. C11 value-predicate behaviour under Arch: in-place mutation without publish does NOT move membership; Set/NotifyChanged does; GravitySystem/MasterRenderSystem behaviour tests. C12 every Arch/facade process-wide static in ProcessWideState; hygiene tests extended; leaking tests fixed. C13 IsAlive/Entity.Null/recycled-id covered by facade tests. C14 guard forbids raw Arch outside facade. C15 gate ×5 + seeded + 6/6 demos + Blender_Level + Level_0 + .mdscene round-trip + web build + pointer-replay diff explained. C16 benchmarks wave-2 vs wave-0 in PR. C17 hot systems converted, behaviour tests green, regressions reverted/justified. C18 gate ×5 + demos green. C19 zero DefaultEcs tokens in git-tracked files except CHANGELOG/ecs-migration/README credits. C20 manifest-honesty green all modules. C21 #118 residue retired, seeded harness kept. C22 docs deliverables land; every premise naming DefaultEcs rewritten/removed in same PR; CHANGELOG Breaking with *Migration:* per break; docs/ecs-migration.md exists. C23 #117 closed; upstream note posted.

## 6. Precondition diff (DefaultEcs semantics → facade guarantees)

Set<T>(v): add-or-update → add-or-update (never Arch's update-only). Structural change mid-iteration: tolerated → tolerated (snapshot iteration). Query membership: maintained sets, predicate re-eval on publish → identical, facade-fired. Changed payload: (entity, old, new); NotifyChanged ⇒ old==new → identical. World components: native Get/Has/Set/Remove + notifications → singleton entity per world, same API + notifications; Set-when-present ⇒ Changed. Iteration order: sparse-set/insertion-ish → unspecified; systems needing order sort explicitly. IsAlive: version-checked handle → same observable semantics. Message bus: typed + [Subscribe] scan → identical, facade-owned, per-world. ReadAllComponents: generic OnRead<T> → same port, registry/reflection-backed, AOT-safe. Process statics: untracked → every facade/Arch static in ProcessWideState.

## 7. Verification protocol

core-first build; dotnet test monodreams.sln Release -m:1 -p:RestoreDisableParallel=true ×5 on wave-close; MONODREAMS_TEST_SEED=8 run; 6 demo screens headless --frames 600; web head build -p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web; MONODREAMS_SCREENSHOT=png TARGET=Main fixed-resolution evidence; pointer-replay vs main baseline diffed and explained; git grep for conflict markers before every commit; never stage .worktrees/."}

# Migrate the ECS backend from DefaultEcs to Arch, behind a MonoDreams-owned facade

**Origem:** https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/issues/119 (the issue is the complete brief; this plan is the issue plus live-codebase verification deltas — where they disagree, the plan wins because it was measured)
**Branch sugerida:** `issue-119-wave0` → `issue-119-wave1` → `issue-119-wave2` → `issue-119-wave3` → `issue-119-wave4` — five stacked branches, one PR per wave (issue §10: "Each wave is its own PR. Do not squash waves together.").
**Domínios:** foundation (sensitive), all 14 modules, examples, cli, platform, tests
**Tier de risco:** deep-plan — engine-wide flow replacement crossing all 14 modules, rooted in sensitive foundation.

## 1. Context

DefaultEcs (pinned 0.18.0-beta01) is unmaintained and carries a live correctness bug (#117: EntityQueryFilterFactory cache-key collision; #118 landed a workaround). The decision (issue #119): ship (1) MonoDreams.Ecs, an engine-owned facade in MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ (namespace MonoDreams.Ecs) that becomes the ONLY ECS surface for every other module, Examples, Demos, CLI-scaffolded games and tests; then (2) swap the facade's backend from DefaultEcs to Arch (https://github.com/genaray/Arch). Behaviour preserved; only ECS plumbing moves. Non-goals: gameplay/module logic rewrites, component-shape changes, Arch.Relationships/Persistence, renderer changes. Read issue #119 §1–§5 (gh issue view 119 --repo roo-oliv/monodreams) for the full measured API-usage table and hazards H1–H10.

Key hazards from the issue: H1 Set semantics invert (DefaultEcs Set = add-or-update; Arch Set = update-only, Add = add-only; 1826 call sites); H2 structural changes during iteration unsafe in Arch (archetype moves); H3 no persistent EntitySet in Arch; H4 iteration order changes (sparse-set → archetype/chunk); H5 no world components in Arch; H6 entity handle lifetime/IsAlive; H7 Arch's reactive events are compiled out of the published NuGet (#if EVENTS) — silent no-op; H8 managed (class) components land in object arrays; H9 Arch keeps static World.Worlds registry + component-type statics (same shape as the #117/#118 flake); H10 world construction args differ entirely.

# Migrate the ECS backend from DefaultEcs to Arch, behind a MonoDreams-owned facade

**Origem:** https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/issues/119 (the issue is the complete brief; this plan is the issue plus live-codebase verification deltas — where they disagree, the plan wins because it was measured)
**Branch sugerida:** `issue-119-wave0` → `issue-119-wave1` → `issue-119-wave2` → `issue-119-wave3` → `issue-119-wave4` — five stacked branches, one PR per wave (issue §10: "Each wave is its own PR. Do not squash waves together.").
**Domínios:** foundation (sensitive), all 14 modules, examples, cli, platform, tests
**Tier de risco:** deep-plan — engine-wide flow replacement crossing all 14 modules, rooted in sensitive foundation.

## 1. Context

DefaultEcs (pinned 0.18.0-beta01) is unmaintained and carries a live correctness bug (#117: EntityQueryFilterFactory cache-key collision; #118 landed a workaround). **Origem:** https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/issues/119 (the issue is the complete brief; this plan is the issue plus live-codebase verification deltas — where they disagree, the plan wins because it was measured)
**Branch sugerida:** `issue-119-wave0` → `issue-119-wave1` → `issue-119-wave2` → `issue-119-wave3` → `issue-119-wave4` — five stacked branches, one PR per wave (issue §10: "Each wave is its own PR. Do not squash waves together.").
**Domínios:** foundation (sensitive), all 14 modules, examples, cli, platform, tests
**Tier de risco:** deep-plan — engine-wide flow replacement crossing all 14 modules, rooted in sensitive foundation.

## 1. Context

DefaultEcs (pinned 0.18.0-beta01) is unmaintained and carries a live correctness bug (#117: EntityQueryFilterFactory cache-key collision; #118 landed a workaround). The decision (issue #119): ship (1) MonoDreams.Ecs, an engine-owned facade in MonoDreams/foundation/Ecs/ (namespace MonoDreams.Ecs) that becomes the ONLY ECS surface for every other module, Examples, Demos, CLI-scaffolded games and tests; then (2) swap the facade's backend from DefaultEcs to Arch (https://github.com/genaray/Arch). Behaviour preserved; only ECS plumbing moves. Non-goals: gameplay/module logic rewrites, component-shape changes, Arch.Relationships/Persistence, renderer changes. Read issue #119 §1–§5 (gh issue view 119 --repo roo-oliv/monodreams) for the full measured API-usage table and hazards H1–H10.

Key hazards from the issue: H1 Set semantics invert (DefaultEcs Set = add-or-update; Arch Set = update-only, Add = add-only; 1826 call sites); H2 structural changes during iteration unsafe in Arch (archetype moves); H3 no persistent EntitySet in Arch; H4 iteration order changes (sparse-set → archetype/chunk); H5 no world components in Arch; H6 entity handle lifetime/IsAlive; H7 Arch's reactive events are compiled out of the published NuGet (#if EVENTS) — silent no-op; H8 managed (class) components land in object arrays; H9 Arch keeps static World.Worlds registry + component-type statics (same shape as the #117/#118 flake); H10 world construction args differ entirely.

## 2. Verification deltas (measured on main @ 7b2cbe2a, 2026-08-18)

### 2a. Surfaces the issue's table MISSES (each needs a facade shape)
